notices.html: Von Thun Farms' Fall Festival is pricier in October: expect about $24.99 per person online or $27.99 at the door for the Oct 3-4 weekend, up from September's rate. Online tickets are recommended to guarantee entry.

No apple picking at Terhune or Battleview again this year: the April freeze wiped out roughly 78% of NJ's apple crop statewide, so both farms are pumpkins and flowers only. Lee Turkey and Johnson's Corner still have apples.
Polar Express train rides are already booking for late November and December: Whippany and Phillipsburg both have 2026 dates on sale now and popular weekends sell out early.

blurbs.terhune: This weekend: Fall Family Fun Weekends continues both days, 10am to 5pm, with the pumpkin patch, corn maze, hay-bale maze, late-morning wagon rides and the animal barnyard. Apple picking is still out for the season after the spring freeze, so it's pumpkins, gourds and flowers instead. Tickets run $19.95 per person online or $24.95 at the door, kids under 3 free. Call 609-924-2310 to confirm before you go.
blurbs.leeturkey: This weekend: apples are still coming in along with the last of the PYO vegetables. We found conflicting picking hours this week, some sources say fields close around 5:15pm and others say 6pm, so call 609-448-0629 to confirm hours and what's ripe before you head over. Still a simple, no-frills farm with no festival extras.
blurbs.vonthun: This weekend: the Fall Festival is in full swing with the corn maze, hayrides, pedal karts, duck races and pumpkin patch, both days 10am to 5pm, last ticket sold at 4pm. October pricing is higher than September's, plan on roughly $24.99 per person online or $27.99 at the door, and book online since fall weekends can sell out. Call 732-329-8656 to confirm before you go.
blurbs.emerys: This weekend: two corn mazes are running, the 2-acre Treasure Hunt maze for younger kids and a bigger 5-acre maze with a clue game for older ones, plus a straw-bale maze and pumpkin display, daily 10am to 5pm with hayrides on weekends. U-pick blueberry season is long over, but fresh berries and their pies are still in the farm market. Call 609-758-8514 to confirm before you go.
blurbs.battleview: This weekend: still no pick-your-own tree fruit after the spring freeze wiped out apples, cherries, peaches and nectarines, but pumpkin picking and weekend hayrides continue and there's a sunflower field for cutting your own. We found conflicting hours this week, so call 732-462-0756 to confirm current hours and crop before you go.
blurbs.johnsons: This weekend: the Fall Harvest Festival continues through October 31 (plus Columbus Day) with apple and pumpkin picking (pumpkins run about $0.99 a pound), a family corn maze on weekends, gem mining, duck races and live music from noon to 4pm on weekends. We couldn't confirm this week's hayride ticket price, last known was $10 online or $12 at the door, so call the Pick Your Own Hotline 609-654-5894 to confirm before you go.
blurbs.dinosafari: This weekend: still closed for the season, since it only ran July 1 through August 16. It's expected to return next summer, so there's no need for a special trip until then.
blurbs.gfs: This weekend: don't miss Family Open Studios: Dino Design on Saturday, 11am to 3pm, a free hands-on dinosaur art workshop included with admission, alongside the Shantell Martin mural exhibit and the usual roaming peacocks and sculpture grounds.
blurbs.lsc: This weekend: the reopened Jennifer Chalsty Planetarium with new laser projectors is running regular weekend hours, 10am to 5pm, still the biggest planetarium in the hemisphere. Book timed tickets online first.
blurbs.sixflags: This weekend: Fright Fest is running, daytime rides are fine for kids 9 to 10, but evening haunted mazes and scare zones start around 6pm and lean older. Plan an earlier visit and head out before dark if that's a concern.
blurbs.diggerland: This weekend: the Diggerfest fall festival is included with general admission, along with Dig or Treat weekend-morning trick-or-treating and a costume parade, both continuing through early November.
blurbs.sesame: This weekend: The Count's Halloween Spooktacular is running with trick-or-treating, a parade, dance parties and a scarecrow scavenger hunt on select dates through November 1. Hours vary by day, so check before you go.

events.title: Hightstown Harvest Festival
events.desc: A free small-town harvest street fair a few minutes from home, with local vendors, food and family activities right on Bank Street.

events.title: Family Open Studios: Dino Design
events.desc: A dinosaur-themed hands-on art workshop for kids, included with admission to the 42-acre sculpture park.

events.title: Shady Brook Farm FallFest
events.desc: A bigger, ticketed Bucks County fall festival with obstacle courses, go-karts, an orchard and a pumpkin patch, a step up in scale from a local farm outing.

events.title: Corn Maze at Howell Living History Farm
events.place: Howell Living History Farm, Lambertville area
events.desc: Run the corn maze, then wander a working 1900s living-history farm with animals and demonstrations, a low-key outdoor day. Sources disagreed on exact hours this week, so call ahead.
